video.title: Color Scheme, Dismiss Action & Environment Value | Day 140
video.description:
Learn to explain how a SwiftUI view reads shared information: Color Scheme, Dismiss Action & Environment Value, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Color Scheme - The setting that tells whether the app looks light or dark.
Dismiss Action - An action that closes the current sheet or screen.
Environment Value - A piece of shared information that SwiftUI keeps for every view, such as the locale.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 140 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Color Scheme, Dismiss Action and Environment Value in English?

dialogue.title: Dark mode and a close button

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my card looks bad in dark mode. How do I check the mode?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Read the Color Scheme from the environment, like `scheme` in the code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is an Environment Value. SwiftUI keeps it for you, and any view can read it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Many. For example the locale, the font size and the Dismiss Action.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does the Dismiss Action do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You call `dismiss()` to close the current sheet or screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I set the Color Scheme to dark with my own property, but it never changed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You cannot write it. It is an Environment Value that comes from the system.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I only read the Color Scheme, and use `dismiss` to close.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Read the Environment Value, and call the Dismiss Action when the user taps Close.
Check the Color Scheme for dark mode.
